project.name: agentic-sam3-annotator
project.description: Agentic SAM3 auto-annotation lab with multi-agent QA and exporters.

nodes.name: base_agent.py
nodes.summary: Abstract base class defining the agent contract for multi-agent annotation conversations, requiring should_respond and respond methods.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ABC pattern with abstract respond method for polymorphic agent dispatch.

nodes.name: BaseAgent
nodes.summary: Abstract agent base storing a name and defining the should_respond/respond interface used by the orchestrator conversation loop.

nodes.name: coordinator_agent.py
nodes.summary: Coordinator agent that drives the annotation workflow by routing actions between SAM3 segmentation and curation QA stages based on bundle state.

nodes.name: CoordinatorAgent
nodes.summary: Workflow coordinator extending BaseAgent; emits ConversationMessage actions to trigger annotation, QA, retry, or terminal states per image bundle.

nodes.name: curation_agent.py
nodes.summary: Quality-assurance agent that validates mask annotations, runs geometry checks, optionally captions images, and produces QAResult decisions.

nodes.name: CurationAgent
nodes.summary: QA agent performing mask quality checks (area, overlap, class balance), optional caption verification, and emitting structured QAResult actions.

nodes.name: sam3_agent.py
nodes.summary: SAM3 segmentation agent that responds to annotate actions by invoking text or exemplar prompts and returning generated MaskRecord payloads.

nodes.name: SAM3Agent
nodes.summary: Segmentation agent wrapping SAM3 text and exemplar prompt APIs to produce MaskRecord instances from coordinator annotate requests.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic data models for project configuration, image/mask records, QA results, conversation messages, and annotation bundles shared across agents.
nodes.languageNotes: Pydantic BaseModel classes with model_dump serialization used throughout the agent pipeline.

nodes.name: ProjectConfig
nodes.summary: Central configuration model holding dataset paths, label schema, SAM3/LLM settings, QA thresholds, and export options for the annotation pipeline.

nodes.name: ImageRecord
nodes.summary: Represents a discovered dataset image with dimensions, path, and metadata used as the anchor for per-image annotation bundles.

nodes.name: MaskRecord
nodes.summary: Stores a single segmentation mask with polygon, bounding box, class ID, confidence, and provenance metadata.

nodes.name: QAResult
nodes.summary: Quality-assurance outcome capturing score, issue list, retry/accept decision, and per-class refinement hints for an image.

nodes.name: ConversationMessage

nodes.name: AnnotationBundle

nodes.name: orchestrator.py
nodes.summary: Main pipeline orchestrator that discovers images, runs multi-agent conversations per bundle in parallel, exports YOLO labels, and writes QA/conversation logs.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: Start here at main.py, the command-line front door for the entire annotation lab. This module parses CLI flags, loads the project YAML, interprets free-text annotation prompts, configures logging, and hands control to the orchestrator pipeline. Understanding main.py shows how a single run command fans out into config loading, prompt planning, and parallel multi-agent processing.
tour.languageLesson: Python's argparse module defines a declarative CLI: add_argument calls register flags and positional args, while a main() guard (`if __name__ == '__main__'`) keeps the entry point import-safe for tests.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README documents the same architecture you just traced from main.py: User → GUI/CLI → CoordinatorAgent → SAM3Agent/CurationAgent → YOLO and LabelMe export. It covers installation, SAM3 weight setup, run commands, output artifacts (qa_report.json, conversation logs), and the annotation state machine (NEW → ANNOTATED → ACCEPTED/QA_RETRY → export or HUMAN_REVIEW). Keep this open as a roadmap while exploring the code.

tour.title: Project Configuration
tour.description: Before the pipeline runs, config_loader.py reads the YAML project file into a typed ProjectConfig Pydantic model, validating required sections like label schema and dataset paths. The example YAML shows every tunable knob—SAM3 backend choice, QA thresholds, LLM settings, and YOLO export mode—so you can see exactly what main.py loads on startup.
tour.languageLesson: YAML configuration files separate runtime settings from code. PyYAML loads the raw dict, then Pydantic validates and coerces it into typed models—catching misconfiguration before any images are processed.

tour.title: Shared Data Models
tour.description: models.py is the most depended-upon module in the codebase, defining the shared vocabulary every layer speaks: ProjectConfig, ImageRecord, MaskRecord, QAResult, ConversationMessage, and AnnotationBundle. These Pydantic models enforce the contract between agents, the orchestrator, exporters, and the GUI. When you read any agent or tool, the types here tell you what data flows where.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic BaseModel classes provide runtime validation and serialization. Field defaults, validators, and model_config let you express domain constraints declaratively instead of scattering if-checks across the codebase.

tour.title: Pipeline Orchestrator
tour.description: The orchestrator is the heart of the system: it discovers images, spins up a ThreadPool for parallel bundle processing, and runs the multi-agent conversation loop for each image. After agents finish, it exports YOLO labels, writes qa_report.json, and saves conversation logs. This file connects every major subsystem—agents, captioning, and YOLO export—into one end-to-end pipeline.

tour.title: Multi-Agent Chatroom
tour.description: The agent layer implements the README's multi-agent chatroom pattern. BaseAgent defines the conversation contract (should_respond and respond), CoordinatorAgent routes workflow actions based on bundle state, SAM3Agent generates masks from text or exemplar prompts, and CurationAgent validates annotations and returns QA decisions. Together they drive each image through the NEW → ANNOTATED → ACCEPTED/QA_RETRY state machine.
tour.languageLesson: Python abstract base classes (ABC) with @abstractmethod enforce a shared interface. Each concrete agent inherits BaseAgent and implements should_respond/respond, enabling polymorphic dispatch in the orchestrator's conversation loop.

tour.title: SAM3 Segmentation Backends
tour.description: When SAM3Agent receives an annotate action, it calls into the SAM3 tools layer. The client module provides a unified API with mock, hosted HTTP, and Hugging Face backends—supporting offline development and production segmentation. The HF backend loads facebook/sam3 via transformers for real local inference, returning polygon detections with bounding boxes that become MaskRecord objects in the bundle.

tour.title: QA Validation Tools
tour.description: CurationAgent relies on the tools layer for quality checks beyond simple accept/reject. geometry.py computes mask area, IoU, and bounding-box overlap for duplicate and empty-mask detection, while captioning.py provides placeholder captions for caption-consistency QA. These utilities translate raw MaskRecord data into the metrics that drive QAResult decisions and retry logic.

tour.title: Prompt Interpreter
tour.description: Both the CLI and GUI accept free-text prompts like 'annotate all cars and pedestrians.' The prompt interpreter converts natural language into a structured PromptPlan with class lists and per-class SAM3 text prompts via synonym expansion and bigram handling. This bridges user intent from main.py and review_app.py into the concrete segmentation prompts SAM3Agent executes.

tour.title: YOLO Label Export
tour.description: Accepted AnnotationBundle records flow into the YOLO exporter, which writes normalized label files and a classes.txt manifest. The exporter supports both bounding-box and polygon segmentation formats, producing the training-ready artifacts described in the README's output section. The orchestrator calls export_yolo after all bundles reach terminal states.

tour.title: Tkinter GUI Interface
tour.description: review_app.py provides the GUI alternative to the CLI entry point, with Setup, Run Log, Results, and Labeler tabs. It runs the same orchestrator in a background thread with cancel support and queue-based log streaming. The LabelerPanel offers LabelMe-compatible manual annotation for HUMAN_REVIEW cases, completing the loop from automated segmentation to human correction.

tour.title: Architecture Specification
tour.description: The agent-spec document is the authoritative design reference for everything you've toured: data model definitions, multi-agent chatroom protocol, orchestrator flow diagrams, tools layer responsibilities, and the phased implementation plan. Cross-reference it with the code to see how design intent maps to the modules in src/, and use the exploration notebook for ad-hoc SAM3 and QA experiments outside the main pipeline.
